etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English enjoyen, from Old French enjoier, anjoier, enjoer (“to give joy, receive with joy, rejoice”), equivalent to en- +‎ joy.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To receive pleasure or satisfaction from something.

quote.citation: 1850, [Alfred, Lord Tennyson], In Memoriam, London: Edward Moxon, […], →OCLC, Canto XLVI, page 69:
quote.text: And we shall sit at endless feast,⁠Enjoying each the other’s good;⁠What vaster dream can hit the moodOf Love on earth?

quote.citation: 2013 July-August, Henry Petroski, “Geothermal Energy”, in American Scientist, volume 101, number 4:
quote.text: Energy has seldom been found where we need it when we want it. Ancient nomads, wishing to ward off the evening chill and enjoy a meal around a campfire, had to collect wood and then spend time and effort coaxing the heat of friction out from between sticks to kindle a flame. With more settled people, animals were harnessed to capstans or caged in treadmills to turn grist into meal.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To have the use or benefit of something.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Numbers 36:8:
quote.text: that the children of Israel may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers

quote.citation: 1922, Agatha Christie, “Chapter 17”, in The Secret Adversary:
quote.text: Night and day were the same in this prison room, but Tommy's wrist-watch, which enjoyed a certain degree of accuracy, informed him that it was nine o'clock in the evening.

quote.citation: 1988, Harry G Frankfurt, The importance of what we care about: philosophical essays:
quote.text: This account fails to provide any basis for doubting that animals of subhuman species enjoy the freedom it defines.

quote.citation: 2008, Jonathan Borwein, ‎David Bailey, Mathematics by Experiment:
quote.text: The Indo-Arabic system was introduced into Europe in 1000 CE, but due to resistance from several quarters, centuries elapsed before it finally enjoyed widespread use.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, India) To be satisfied or receive pleasure.

quote.citation: 1667, John Milton, “Book IX”, in Paradise Lost. […], London:  […]  [Samuel Simmons], and are to be sold by Peter Parker […]; [a]nd by Robert Boulter […]; [a]nd Matthias Walker, […], →OCLC; republished as Paradise Lost in Ten Books: […], London: Basil Montagu Pickering […], 1873, →OCLC:
quote.text: Never did thy Beautie […] so enflame my sense With ardor to enjoy thee.
